messages:
Sam Nguyen: FYI seeing a regression on long sequences after the recent positional-kernel switch. Some in-prod requests hit NaNs in attention weights and trigger fallback to CPU.
Nisha Patel: repro? short log or command please.
Sam Nguyen: repro is simple: run the llama-compat benchmark with a mixed batch (one short, one ~6k tokens). Command: `python perf_check.py --model rwlm-7b --batch 2 --lens 256,6144 --fp16`. Fail log: ```attn_kern.cpp:312 numeric overflow: exp produced inf; softmax result contains NaN; fallback applied```
Devon Park: that smells like an FP accumulation order + kernel fusion change. The new kernel does fused dot->scale->apply-rope in a different tree, so rounding differs. fp16 + batching with heterogeneous lengths amplifies it.
Nisha Patel: confirmed locally. If I force bf16 the issue disappears. Also only reproducible when `batch_var` > 0 (i.e., mixed seq lengths). Pure long-batch (all 6k) is fine.
Sam Nguyen: interesting. so two axes: precision (fp16 vs bf16) and batching heterogeneity.
Devon Park: my hypothesis: the fast path rearranged ops to reduce memory traffic (compute scaled qk, then apply ROPE, then softmax). The slow/stable path applies ROPE earlier per head and does per-row normalization. Tiny negative rounding before exp causes large relative change.
Nisha Patel: runtime-bot kicked off a canary CI job: https://ci/redwood/attn/regress/1769991234. It reproduces in HW sim with Ampere T4 fp16 mode.
runtime-bot: CI job queued -> running -> https://ci/redwood/attn/regress/1769991234
Devon Park: possible quick mitigations: (1) clamp logits before exp: `logits = min(logits, MAX_LOGIT)` and `logits = logits - max(logits, axis=-1, keepdims=True)` (2) reorder ops to apply max-subtract earlier (3) switch default for mixed batches to `stable` kernel until we have a fix.
Sam Nguyen: what's perf hit for (3)? we need numbers to make a rollout decision.
Nisha Patel: microbench on an r5g-like instance: `fast_v2` = 1.0x baseline, `stable_v1` = 0.89x for seq>2048. Numbers: ```seq=4096 batch=2 fast_v2: 148 ms/step stable_v1: 166 ms/step```
Devon Park: 12% slower but stable. Another idea: kernel-selection policy could look at per-batch seq variance: if variance > threshold => pick `stable_v1`. That keeps most traffic on fast path.
Sam Nguyen: I like adaptive selection. Also we should add a deterministic accumulation mode for fp16 where we do `accum = fp32(accum)`, keep everything in fp32 for reductions, then cast back — that'll remove rounding non-determinism. Perf cost small relative to full stable kernel.
Nisha Patel: propose immediate plan: 1) revert global default to `fast_v2` only for homogeneous batches; 2) add selection hook: `if batch_var > 512 and any(len>2048): use stable_v1` 3) add a runtime flag `--force-rope-stable` for canary 4) add unit+fuzz tests in CI with mixed-len seeds.
Devon Park: long-term: refactor kernel interface. Right now kernels get a blob of inputs and do everything. We should split into phases: `precompute_posenc()` (sincos/rope tables), `apply_posenc_per_head(q,k)` and `reduce_and_softmax()`. That makes it easier to test and swap single-stage implementations. Also maintain a small "stability contract": kernels must pass a numerical tolerance harness vs float32 reference.
Sam Nguyen: agreed. also need to account for quantization path (int8): some of those fused ops assume symmetric ranges and will exacerbate overflow. Add quant-mode to kernel policy.
Nisha Patel: I'll add a regression test set named `posenc_longtail` with 200 prompts (varied lengths 128..8192, mixed batches). Test checks no NaNs and max rel-diff < 1e-3 vs fp32 reference for logits.
Devon Park: small numeric trick to mitigate immediately: after compute logits do `logits = logits - max(logits, axis=-1)` then `where(isfinite(logits), logits, clamp_val)` and use a small additive epsilon in denominators. Also cap exponent argument: `exp_arg = clamp(exp_arg, -100, 100)`. These are cheap and can be pushed as a hotfix.
Sam Nguyen: let's also add telemetry: count how often kernel falls back to CPU and emit histogram of sequence variance for those requests. Want to see if this is only one customer pattern.
Nisha Patel: action items: - @Devon implement clamp & early max-subtract in `fast_v2` (hotfix) by EOD - @Nisha add `posenc_longtail` CI + canary flag and run on canary cluster - @Sam add kernel-policy PR that picks stable for mixed batches and exposes `--force-rope-stable` runtime override.
Devon Park: I'll also prototype the split-phase API in a branch `kernels/refactor/posenc-phase` and add the fp32 harness.
Sam Nguyen: agreed. please post PR numbers when ready.
Nisha Patel: re: rollout: suggested canary 2% traffic -> monitor CPU fallbacks and NaN rate, if stable after 24h -> 25% -> 100%.
runtime-bot: noted action items and created ticket RW-6122 (attn numeric harness + adaptive policy).
Sam Nguyen: thanks all. keeping this thread open, will paste perf diffs and PRs here. :thumbsup:
